CHIEF COMPLAINT
Difficulty breathing with sports and mood concerns.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a student experiencing exercise-induced asthma symptoms, primarily during aerobic activities and water polo. Symptoms include phlegm buildup in throat, coughing, chest tightness, wheezing, and lightheadedness. Symptoms occur almost every time with aerobic workout. Patient uses albuterol inhaler with two puffs when symptomatic; symptoms improve within 15 minutes after inhaler use. Patient reports tremor/shakiness as a side effect of the inhaler. Patient also experiences coughing when around smoke and avoids such situations. Denies nocturnal symptoms. Currently uses only rescue inhaler, no daily asthma medications.

Regarding mood, patient reports feeling stressed, sad, and lacking motivation recently, which started this year. Patient attributes this to school pressure, SAT studying, and AP classes. Patient experiences fatigue and prefers staying home to going out with friends. Denies specific difficulty with focus or information retention; describes predominantly sadness and lack of motivation.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports seasonal allergies.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Asthma.

MEDICATIONS
Albuterol inhaler (rescue inhaler, two puffs as needed).

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is a student taking AP classes and preparing for SATs. Enjoys water polo and sports.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Heart and lungs: normal. Eyes: normal. Ears: small amount of fluid noted bilaterally. Throat: no tonsils, appears normal. Abdomen: bowel sounds normal, palpation normal. Reflexes: all normal.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Asthma: Will start daily montelukast (Singulair) given possible underlying allergies and frequent exercise-induced symptoms. Patient to continue using albuterol inhaler as needed. Expected improvement within approximately one month. Follow-up visit in six weeks.
2. Mood symptoms: Appears related to academic stress. Will initiate therapy. Patient to complete screening questionnaires. Follow-up in two weeks.
